title: Proficiency scale and evidence ladder
description: Governs content/taxonomy/proficiency.yaml. Defines what each of the five levels means generically, and what evidence is required to attain it. Per-element observable anchors live on the element itself; this file is the frame those anchors are written into. Changing the meaning of a level retroactively changes what every existing credential asserts, so this file is steward-controlled (see GOVERNANCE.md).

descriptor.description: What this level means across all elements, in behavioural terms. The element's own anchor makes it concrete.

assessedAt.description: Scope at which this level is assessed. The shipped rubric uses `element` at every level, so a credential names exactly what was tested: 'CM-03-048 at L2' means that element was assessed, not that some cluster containing it was. An earlier design assessed L1 and L2 across a whole competency area, which was cheaper to author but produced an ambiguous claim — and a credential's meaning cannot be renegotiated once it has been issued. The `competency-area` value is retained so a fork or an organization overlay can make the opposite trade deliberately, but anything using it must say so on the credential.

assessment.description: How competence at this level is demonstrated. Every assessment in this system is OPEN-RESOURCE: the candidate may use references, the internet, and AI assistance, because a working metrologist has all three. There is no proctoring anywhere. Integrity is carried by item design — parameterized problems give every candidate different numbers, so a shared answer key is worthless, and an item answerable by lookup is a defective item.

modality.description: Recorded as visible provenance on the resulting credential, so a reader sees how it was earned rather than having to assume.

requiresWorkProduct.description: An independent work product short of a full capstone — a real deliverable, archived and hashed.

requiresMentoring.description: Demonstrated development of others at L3 or above. Reserved for L5: at expert level, the field's judgement is that you have not mastered something until you can bring someone else to competence in it.

doubleScored.description: Independent scoring by two reviewers with a documented disagreement-resolution path. Applied at L4 and L5 — inter-rater reliability is what makes a credential defensible in an accreditation audit.

minExperienceHours.description: Minimum recorded practice before the level may be claimed. Time cannot be shortcut; this is one of the mechanisms that makes the corpus a lifetime's pursuit rather than a checkbox.

minDaysSincePreviousLevel.description: Mandatory interval after attaining the level below.

signoff.description: Who attests. NO SELF-SIGNOFF EVER, at any level: the signer must be a distinct natural person who witnessed the output.

witnessMustHoldLevel.description: Minimum level the signer must hold in this same element. Null at L1 and L2 — a witness attests that they saw the work, which does not require them to be more expert than the candidate. From L3 the signer must be a credentialed reviewer holding at least this level, because they are now judging quality rather than merely observing.

requiresCredentialedReviewer.description: Signer must additionally hold the reviewer-competence credential covering review methodology, rubric calibration, and bias.

requiresCrossOrganizational.description: At least one signer must be outside the candidate's own organization. Applied at L5 to prevent a closed group from certifying its own experts.

defaultRecertificationMonths.description: Default currency period at this level, overridable per element.
